**BPO Architect — Final WP6 and BPOT Findings Disposition**

I have reviewed all 14 proposed template improvements.

**Decisions:**

- Approve items 1–4 for the first post-WP6 release.
- Approve item 5, with separate finding-validity, origin, and resolution fields, coordinated with P5.
- Approve item 6 for reproducibility improvements.
- Approve items 7–9 as controlled, lower-priority enhancements.
- Approve item 10 as documentation of definition provenance, without treating project authorship as an external definition source.
- Approve item 11 after dependency locking.
- Approve item 12 and elevate it to the next governance-improvement cycle, coordinated with P5.
- Reject items 13 and 14.

Retain the previously accepted low-priority disposition for SDD domain/range validation under Decision 28.

**WP6 closure:** I accept the reported verdict under Decision 27 and authorize WP6 closeout once the final evaluation artifacts, comparison evidence, finding dispositions, and reproducibility record are confirmed. Check that unavailable validation rungs were not represented as zero findings.

**Commit `4ac2eaf`:** Approved for push and normal review.

Do not implement the 12 approved improvements before closing WP6. Transfer them to a prioritized post-WP6 improvement backlog.

Our experimental objective was to determine whether applying the Ontology Template surfaces modeling and engineering gaps and produces measurable quality improvements.

The findings demonstrate meaningful detection capability and identify weaknesses in the template itself. Those weaknesses are outcomes of the evaluation, not reasons to restart it.

**The next phase is template improvement informed by WP6, not continued WP6 experimentation.**

Please complete the closeout record, preserve the accepted results, and begin the first post-WP6 release under this prioritized scope.
